assessment: All original 7070 noon observations per asset/date, 42420 distinct rows across three exposed dates. Retain all 73 sources registered in the transformer screen, irrespective of their as-yet unseen scores. For each of ten new trajectory outputs per date, retain standalone forecasts and fixed 50/50 blends with the historical matched-representation HGB and deep500_hgb.
clock: Reset from the original checkpoint at 11:00 each date. At each integer UTC minute 11:00 through 13:59, train using source decisions in the previous 1800 seconds whose actual future quote time plus 100ms is at or before that minute. Publish that update ten seconds later; the previous model supplies all predictions before publication. Each update must complete within the fixed ten-second allowance. Preserve and reject any timing violation as operationally infeasible rather than changing its delay after scores. No current or future label may enter its own prediction.
feedback_semantics: Canonical actual future_event_time plus a separately imposed 100ms observation allowance. Window age is measured from source decision time. Every query retains its original five-second exact label. Earlier assessment outcomes may train later forecasts only after release; this is a prequential deployment procedure, not an independent row-by-row fixed-model test.
hypothesis: Within-session supervised adaptation can track changing feature/target relationships that fixed noon checkpoints and prior-only updates cannot. Historical class-balanced replay may constrain forgetting. This is delayed-feedback supervised learning, with prediction before feedback, and is distinct from the completed pre-noon fine-tuning and three-bias calibration studies.
optimization: One AdamW step per minute on the exact aggregate gradient (1-replay_weight)*L_recent + replay_weight*L_historical. Accumulate losses in batches of 1024 with each batch sum divided by its full cohort size, then clip gradient norm at five and step once. Full-network weight decay .01. The bias control freezes all original parameters and updates a zero-initialized 2-by-3 asset-specific logit offset with zero weight decay. Adam state persists within one date only. CPU two threads, deterministic seed 20260908. No epoch selection, validation-based tuning or stopping based on assessment performance.
prediction: Natural probabilities always use original per-asset training priors after softmax of current logits and optional bias. Zero adaptation uses the original full-noon prediction path and must reproduce saved forecasts exactly. Changing future features or not-yet-released labels must leave earlier adaptive predictions unchanged, including during the ten-second publication interval.
primary_policy: Unchanged prediction-only one-hour prior adaptation initialized from the same pre-noon prior. Secondary registered policy uses the same common full historical observations_tree prior for new outputs; preserve old controls exactly.

primary_sources.scope: Pham et al. motivate combining fast adaptation and stored past knowledge in online forecasting. This proposed update is not their FSNet architecture.

Csaba et al. explicitly separate delayed label arrival from current input arrival and study memory replay. Their vision-stream gains do not transfer to this market task; our replay is class-balanced historical sampling, not their importance-weighted feature matching.
Kim et al. motivate test-time forecasting adaptation with newly observed outcomes. Our three-class target has a single full future release; no partially observed target is substituted.

promotion: Exposed-date development only. Any promising result needs a separately frozen independent-date confirmation of the complete causal online procedure, including warmup, delayed feedback, replay and publication timing. No generic online-learning theorem guarantees market improvement or removes date dependence.
recent_objective: Compute class frequencies using only the released 30-minute window, separately per asset. The original network logits z recover natural probabilities as normalize(softmax(z)*pi_original). Therefore recent balanced CE uses logits z + log(pi_original) - log(pi_recent), with weight N/(6*n_asset_class) per example. This preserves the original inference posterior contract while fitting the recent population. Skip an update, for every corresponding variant, if any asset/class cell is absent.
replay: Draw one immutable historical bank of at most 6144 unique rows, equal counts in each asset/class cell, from the same original four-day training cohort using seed 20260908. Retain original cohort priors. Under this stratified sampling, unweighted CE on original logits z estimates the original equal-asset/class objective; do not replace the original prior by the bank sampling prior. Use every bank row when replay_weight=.5.
starting_checkpoints: Exact existing single-member 64-by-64 observations_neural and combined_neural checkpoints, fitted on d-5 through d-2 with the previous noon for epoch selection. Their training-only normalizers, feature schemas and original asset priors remain fixed.
validation: Verify exact class-weighted loss and replay gradients against full-cohort calculations; original/recent logit rebasing; strict release and publication clocks; unchanged forecasts under future-label and future-feature perturbations; prefix behavior; zero-adaptation parity; serialization of network, bias and optimizer state; a finite synthetic delayed-feedback adaptation. Freeze final source/data/checkpoint hashes after implementation and tests. Run after the current transformer family finishes, one substantial learner at a time. Complete all three new trajectories families before inspecting any new scores.
